purpose: Determine whether the small one-factor deltas reflect a real heuristic contribution, run instability, or selection-path noise.

runtime_gate.policy: No follow-up controller may start until this record is complete.

studies.description: Run the tuned heuristic twice with identical profiles and runner settings.
studies.interpretation: Compare paired unresolved-state prefixes first. After the first changed selection or state, step counts are descriptive rather than causal.

studies.description: Run only one semantic signal family at a time: keywords, relevant paths, high-risk paths, or risky words. Buildability and feedback remain enabled.
studies.interpretation: A factor is useful only if it improves matched-prefix ranking or repeatable outcomes across cases; one unusually short run is insufficient.

studies.description: Replace each issue's signal family with a deterministic signal family from another scoped-10 issue, with no self-match.
studies.interpretation: This negative control preserves signal-count scale while breaking issue-specific alignment. A result similar to the tuned baseline indicates weak issue-specific signal value.

historical_evidence.coverage: 6 of 10 issues have complete historical one-factor arms; these runs have non-matched dates and are not the confirmatory result.
historical_evidence.pairing_rule: Only the common prefix with identical unresolved state and selected SHA is paired; all later steps are excluded from causal delta claims.
